overall_summary: Analysis across 47 deduplicated shorts reveals a stark performance divergence. High-concept, visceral 'What If You Fell Into...' cosmic survival hooks and extreme planetary anomalies consistently lead the channel (averaging 800-1,050+ views with 3.5%+ like ratios and viewer comments), whereas recycled cognitive psychology facts and flat trivia re-uploads ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') suffer catastrophic fatigue, stalling below 50 views. Longer formats (19–21 seconds) vastly outperform ultra-short 12–15 second uploads by providing enough pacing for sensory storytelling and tension.

winning_patterns.pattern: Visceral first-person survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') on lethal cosmic environments
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes, 2 comments), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate top retention and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, first-person perspective 'What If You Fell Into/Onto...' formats combining extreme physics with visceral physical consequences.

winning_patterns.pattern: Mind-bending exoplanetary paradoxes with strong visual hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,027 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views, 21 likes) generated the highest velocity relative to publication recency.
winning_patterns.action: Pair extreme cosmic statistics with cinematic micro-visual hooks emphasizing impossible natural physics.

winning_patterns.pattern: 21-second retention structure with a mid-video twist
winning_patterns.evidence: Every single video hitting over 700 views has a runtime of 19 to 21 seconds, while sub-16 second shorts averaged under 120 views.
winning_patterns.action: Lock default Shorts pacing to 19–21 seconds, using seconds 0–3 for immediate sensory danger and seconds 10–14 for the escalating physical reality.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded multiple times garnered 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' flopped at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Immediately cease re-uploading generic neuroscience and cognitive trivia; audience views these as sterile textbook facts.

weak_patterns.pattern: Static observational titles lacking personal threat or tension
weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' pulled only 10 views and 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' got 11 views, despite having space subject matter.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive documentary phrasing ('The Planet Where...'); reframe into active conflict, consequence, or direct second-person immersion.
